change.title: feat: approve agent sign-ins on app.t3.codes with T3 Connect (#33632)
change.description: feat: approve agent sign-ins on app.t3.codes with T3 Connect (#33632)
change.author: Julius Marminge

findings.title: Non-owner users on the tunnel address are dead-ended: the code fallback link only appears after a successful call
findings.body: The server now sends every non-link sign-in on the linked tunnel host to the hosted `/approve-agent` page (mcpOAuthHttp.ts:128-135), where the old page offered a code field plus an optional hosted sign-in. Here the "Use a sign-in code instead" link renders only when `environment` is set, and `environment` is set only inside `connectTransport.send` after the Connect call succeeds (lines 50-53). If the visitor's Clerk account is not the owner (the usual case for someone using `t3 auth pairing create` or a Settings code), `load` fails, McpConsent shows 'This sign-in cannot continue … start the sign-in again from your agent', and the footer holds only 'Use another account'. A code-holding user on the tunnel address previously could approve and now has no link back to `<tunnel>/connect-agent` from the page. Have the server pass the environment's own approval-page URL (or the tunnel origin) in the redirect, or derive the fallback without waiting for a successful call.

findings.title: Every failure is mapped to ConnectMcpApprovalUnavailableError, which makes the web fallback message dead and the wording wrong
findings.body: `Effect.mapError` wraps all failures (timeout, relay blip, 5xx, DPoP rejection, 'rejected the renewed session authorization') in an error whose message says 'Could not reach that environment through T3 Connect with this account.' ApproveAgentSurface.tsx:45-47 then branches on `isUnavailable`, but the other branch ('Could not reach this environment. Try again.') can never be taken for a typed failure. A timeout on the decision POST reads as a reachability/ownership problem, though the decision may have been applied. Either keep the typed causes distinct (timeout vs. not-owner) or drop the dead branch.

findings.title: Is the CSRF token still valid if the DPoP token is renewed between approval and decision?
findings.body: `csrfToken` is signed over `session.sessionId` (McpOAuth.ts:310-319) and `approve` compares it with the session of the decision request (McpOAuth.ts:471-475). `executeEnvironmentRequest` renews the token and retries on `invalid_credential` (environmentHttpAuth.ts:233-241), and `getDpopToken` renews near expiry. If a renewed relay token maps to a different session id, a user who leaves the consent page open past the token lifetime gets 'Your session cannot approve this request. Enter a pairing code instead.' on a page that has no code field (acceptsCode is false). I did not read how the relay issues sessions or how long the token lives. Does the session id survive renewal? If not, the decision path should reload the approval, or the page should offer a retry.

findings.title: The deleted Connect tests were not replaced for the new transport
findings.body: The old test covered the one safety property of the previous flow (never act for a different origin). The new module has none: the unauthorized-response detection (`csrfToken === undefined` as stale credential, lines 95-97), the `refused` mapping of AuthMcpApprovalError, and the redirect/details answers are untested. AGENTS.md lists auth guards among the behavior that needs tests. A test with a stubbed `RemoteEnvironmentAuthorization` and fetch, as the deleted peerPairingCode.test.ts did, would cover the stale-credential retry and the refusal.

findings.title: A second hosted-app URL config that only differs by default, used by one call site
findings.body: `agentApprovalAppUrlConfig` reads the same `T3CODE_HOSTED_APP_URL` as `hostedAppUrlConfig` but defaults to nightly. A nightly build now sends approvals to nightly.app.t3.codes while `McpOAuth.layerMcpClientAuthenticator` (McpOAuth.ts:590) and `CliTokenManager` (CliTokenManager.ts:514) still use app.t3.codes for the same build. If nightly hosted-app routing is wanted for the whole build, change the default of `hostedAppUrlConfig`; if only this page needs it, say why in a comment. The nightly default has no test in publicConfig.test.ts.

findings.title: Approval no longer requires a browser cookie session
findings.body: `approvingSession` uses `authenticateHttpRequest`, so any non-MCP session holding `access:write` and `orchestration:read` (cookie, bearer, or DPoP) can read a CSRF token and approve. MCP-client sessions are still rejected by `authenticateToken`'s caller path (rejectMcpClientAudience), and the decision's scopes are still bounded by the session's own scopes (line 475). The widening is what the hosted flow needs. The test at McpOAuth.test.ts:734-744 covers the bearer success case, but none shows a bearer lacking those scopes is refused; the existing reader case covers only the cookie path.

findings.title: Hosted wizard drops the remote-clients / Manage-access messages the Access step showed
findings.body: When `mcpHostedApproval` is true the Access step is skipped, so `useGrantableLevels` (line 209) is no longer shown. That hook is where this wizard told the user "This device needs the Manage access permission" or that a managed policy keeps remote clients out (line 215). The Connect step now just says to approve on the sign-in page. I could not find the server code that refuses a browser-session approval under a `remoteClients` policy; it is not in `apps/server/src/auth/*.ts`. If it does not refuse, the policy is bypassed. If it does refuse, the user only finds out after the agent has opened the page. Does the hosted flow enforce `remoteClients` server-side, and does the page show why it refuses?

findings.title: Hosted wizard promises a no-code sign-in, but the server can fall back to the code-only page
findings.body: The wizard decides on the capability flag alone (line 125) and shows "approve with your T3 Connect account" with no code. `hostedApprovalUrl` in `apps/server/src/auth/mcpOAuthHttp.ts:78-93` only redirects to the hosted app when the link state is linked, not revoked, and the tunnel hostname matches the issuer. It also returns none on any link-state error (`orElseSucceed(Option.none)`) and for peer-link clients (line 129). In those cases the agent lands on `/connect-agent`, which has only the code field, and the wizard never offered a code. The page's hint names other places to get one (Settings → Sharing & access), so the user can recover. A short fallback line or a collapsed "Get code" under the hosted copy would avoid the dead end.

findings.title: "Approving without a code starts at Read only" is no longer true for the hosted page
findings.body: The T3 Connect page now uses `requireLevelChoice`, so it opens with no level selected and the button reads "Choose what it may do" (`ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:152-159`, `366-367`). Only the environment's own page falls back to Read only (`resolveMcpAccess`). The paragraph at lines 72-75 describes the pre-change defaults (Auto, Read only) for both pages. Say that the T3 Connect page starts with nothing selected.

contracts.action: Approve an agent sign-in from the hosted app with the owner's T3 Connect session (load details, then send the decision)
contracts.equivalent_path: ConnectAgentSurface primaryTransport (apps/web/src/components/auth/ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:108-115): same-origin cookie call to /oauth/mcp/approval and /decision, then McpConsent.
contracts.before_after: Before: hosted app minted a one-use approval code and returned it in a URL fragment to the env page. Now: the hosted app calls approval/decision directly on the relay address with DPoP headers; server approvingSession authenticates the request, computes the CSRF token from the session id and request, and approve() mints the auth code and redirects to the agent's redirect URI. Same server approve() as the cookie path.
contracts.visible_effect: McpConsent renders the consent screen with the environment label; on decision the window follows the redirect through agentRedirectUrl (https or loopback http only).
contracts.failure_mode: Not-owner or unreachable relay, timeouts and refusals all surface as 'This sign-in cannot continue' with only 'Use another account' in the footer; the code-fallback link is absent until a call succeeds. A stuck relay session leaves the 'Connecting to T3 Connect' spinner with no error (ApproveAgentSurface.tsx:121-131).

contracts.action: Server redirects /oauth/mcp/authorize on the linked tunnel host to the hosted /approve-agent page, except for peer-link clients
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous behavior: always redirect to /connect-agent on the environment and offer connectSignIn in the details response.
contracts.before_after: Before: the environment's own page was always the landing page and could hand off to the hosted app. Now: the landing page is the hosted app when the tunnel hostname matches the linked state; linkState failure falls back to the own page (orElseSucceed none). Peer-link clients stay local.
contracts.visible_effect: Browser lands on app.t3.codes (or nightly.app.t3.codes on nightly builds) with the original query plus `environment`.
contracts.failure_mode: A visitor who is not the Connect owner cannot reach the code field from the hosted error state (finding on ApproveAgentSurface.tsx:159). A crafted hosted link naming a peer-link client_id is not blocked by the hosted page, but approve() already allowed session decisions for peer-link clients on the own page.

contracts.action: Bound on the whole Connect approval call (authorizeDpopHttp, request, one renewal retry)
contracts.before_after: The first `authorizeDpopHttp` in callConnectMcpApproval sits outside the 10s timeout but has its own 30s DPOP_AUTHORIZATION_TIMEOUT_MS. The request loop, including at most one renew-and-retry and the second authorizeDpopHttp, sits inside one Effect.timeoutOrElse of 10s. Worst case is about 40s of spinner on the consent page ('Checking the sign-in request' or a pending decision), then the unavailable message.
contracts.visible_effect: The page shows a spinner for up to roughly 40s, then an error that says the environment is unreachable.
contracts.failure_mode: A timed-out decision POST may already have been applied server-side; the user sees an error and can retry, which mints another code (harmless, single-use).

contracts.action: Agent sign-in redirects (load and decision) are now filtered through agentRedirectUrl before window.location.replace
contracts.equivalent_path: Old submitDecision and the load effect called window.location.replace(answer.url) with no check. The server validates the redirect URI at registration in parseRedirect (apps/server/src/auth/McpOAuth.ts:104-116): https, or http on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1].
contracts.before_after: Before: any URL the environment returned was followed. After: only https, or http on a loopback host, is followed; otherwise the page shows UNSAFE_REDIRECT. The client rule matches the server's (isLoopbackHost in packages/shared/src/preview.ts:52 includes "[::1]"), so no legitimate redirect is blocked.
contracts.visible_effect: A hostile or compromised environment cannot send the owner's window to a javascript: or data: URL. On refusal the page shows an error and the buttons come back (setPending(null)).
contracts.failure_mode: The refusal is visible. For a decision that was already accepted server-side, the user sees the error and the agent never gets the code. The server never emits such URLs, so this is unreachable in practice.

contracts.action: Approve is disabled for 700 ms after the page is ready or the window regains focus or visibility
contracts.equivalent_path: No earlier arming. The old page enabled Approve as soon as details loaded and a decision could be built.
contracts.before_after: After: canApprove requires `armed`, which is reset on `focus` and `visibilitychange` and set again by a timer. Deny stays enabled. Enter-submit goes through the same canApprove gate.
contracts.visible_effect: Approve looks disabled for under a second after load or tab switch. There is no explanation on the button.
contracts.failure_mode: The timer and listeners are cleaned up on unmount. If load fails, the status never becomes ready and Approve is never shown. After a failed decision, `armed` stays true, which is correct.

contracts.action: Hosted wizard skips the Access step and shows the Connect step without a code
contracts.equivalent_path: Old path: Access step picks a level, then ApprovalCode mints a level-bound code via mintMcpApprovalCodeOn. The server side (hostedApprovalUrl) redirects /authorize to the hosted app only for a linked tunnel with a matching hostname.
contracts.before_after: mcpUrl always comes from t3ConnectMcpUrl, which is a T3 Connect tunnel hostname, so the issuer normally matches and the redirect applies. Older environments lack the capability and keep the 3-step code flow. In the fallback cases the code-only page appears with no code minted (see finding).
contracts.visible_effect: Two steps (App, Connect). Step clicks map index 1 to the real step 2. The Access-step policy messages are no longer shown.
contracts.failure_mode: If the server falls back to its own page, the user has no code from the wizard. The page's hint names where to get one.
contracts.open_question: Does the server enforce the managed remoteClients policy for a browser-session approval, and does the hosted page tell the user when it refuses?

contracts.action: Hosted page calls the environment through the owner's T3 Connect session (runConnectMcpApproval, connectTransport)
contracts.equivalent_path: Primary page uses runPrimaryHttp with the browser session. The Connect path uses executeAuthenticatedEnvironmentHttpRequest with a DPoP-signed relay credential, and treats details without a csrfToken as an unauthorized response.
contracts.before_after: Results are mapped: success to ok/redirect/refused; any other failure becomes ConnectMcpApprovalUnavailableError and then a user-facing message in ApproveAgentSurface.connectTransport.
contracts.visible_effect: The error text is shown in the "This sign-in cannot continue" screen (on load) or in the form alert (on decision).
contracts.failure_mode: Rejection is mapped to a visible message. Timeout is 10 s. A decision failure leaves the form usable so the user can retry.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** The approach holds together. Server `approvingSession` runs the same `approve()` as before, MCP-client sessions are still rejected, the Connect call is bounded by a 10s timeout plus a 30s token step, and no references to the removed symbols remain. Two things need author attention. A user on the tunnel address who isn't the Connect owner now has no link to the code page from the hosted error state. The new Connect transport has no tests after the old ones were deleted. I also ask whether the CSRF token survives a DPoP token renewal, which I could not settle from the code.

**Batch 2 of 2.** I found nothing that blocks merging this part. The redirect allow-list in the consent page matches the server's registration rule, and the 700 ms arming of Approve is cleaned up on unmount. The mcpHostedApproval wizard has two soft spots. It drops the Access-step policy messages, so I could not confirm the server enforces the remote-clients policy for hosted approvals. It also promises a no-code sign-in even though the server can fall back to the code-only page. The user doc still says approving without a code starts at Read only, but the T3 Connect page now starts with nothing selected. The deleted mint helper and connectAgentApproval have no remaining references in this part or the repository.
